transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 15:00 PT
Duration: 37 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Ariana Chen (Redwood AE), Benji Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (CTO - Lighthouse), Carlos Ruiz (Head of Platform), Olivia Park (ML Eng)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Redwood quickstart + self-serve API, free credits and time-to-first-token, and initial consideration of hosted vs dedicated for a pilot. Customer is evaluating options, primary concerns are cost predictability, latency for embedding workloads, and security (SAML/KMS).

Topics: onboarding flow, free credits, dashboard + tokens, quickstart sample code, benchmarking plan, data residency and SSO, dedicated capacity vs hosted TCO tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Ariana Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ariana from Redwood, this is Benji our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:05] Maya Singh: Hey good, thanks. Excited to learn about the quickstart. We poked around the docs but wanted to get a sense of time-to-first-token for our engineers.
[00:12] Carlos Ruiz: Yup, our platform team will own infra and we want to understand what the self-serve path looks like and whether we can get a pilot up quickly.
[00:18] Benji Patel: Great — that's exactly what we'll cover. Quick note, apologies if audio cuts a bit, we had a little lag on my side.
[00:22] Olivia Park: No worries, can hear you.
[00:24] Ariana Chen: Cool. Quick high level — Redwood offers Hosted API for fastest onboarding, Dedicated for reserved capacity, and Private for VPC/on-prem. Today we'll focus on the hosted quickstart and the steps to move to a Dedicated pilot if you prefer.
[00:36] Maya Singh: Sounds good. Primary use case is embeddings for semantic search across our product docs and support transcripts. Right now we're using OpenAI embeddings and a small Cohere eval, but cost is climbing. We're interested in open models and better unit economics.
[00:50] Benji Patel: Totally. For embeddings the self-serve path is straightforward — sign up, create an API key, run the quickstart script which ships with sample prompts and batching defaults, and you should see first tokens in under a minute if you run local curl or the SDK. Time-to-first-token is usually < 60s from signup to a single call.
[01:05] Carlos Ruiz: When you say "sign up" — do we need to go through any sales to get free credits or is that automatic?
[01:10] Ariana Chen: We have a PLG flow — self-serve signup gives basic credits automatically for evaluation. For pilots we can increase credits programmatically and we also provide a single-click apply for evaluation boosts, plus I can send a promo credit link after this call.
[01:19] Maya Singh: Nice. Are there rate limits on the trial keys that will interfere with a small benchmark?
[01:24] Benji Patel: Trial keys have conservative rate limits to prevent abuse, but for a benchmark you can request a burst increase — we usually coordinate that via an AE. For a proper pilot we recommend a short Dedicated trial or a hosted burst window so you can run realistic QPS.
[01:36] Olivia Park: For our probe, we want to push roughly 1000 embedding requests per second for 30 minutes to approximate peak. Is that feasible on hosted?
[01:44] Benji Patel: Hosted can handle bursts but sustained 1k qps for embeddings might be more predictable on Dedicated — depends on model and quantization. For the quickstart you can prototype with a sampled stream and then scale to a dedicated pool for the real run.
[01:56] Maya Singh: Understood. Can you talk about the SDK and examples? Our engineers prefer Python and we have Node.js too.
[02:02] Ariana Chen: Absolutely — SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. The quickstart repo includes a one-file Python example that installs the SDK, sets REDWOOD_API_KEY, and runs an embeddings call. It also shows batching options and how to enable streaming for text generation.
[02:15] Carlos Ruiz: Do you expose token-level cost breakdowns and dashboards? Our finance folks will want visibility.
[02:20] Benji Patel: Yes — Redwood Console has per-token cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and exportable usage CSVs. We also have tagging for routes so you can attribute spend to teams.
[02:30] Maya Singh: OK. Security is big for us — SSO, audit logs, retention, KMS. Can you run through what's available in Hosted vs Dedicated?
[02:38] Ariana Chen: Hosted supports SAML SSO for enterprise accounts, audit logging, and optional enterprise logging retention. For customer-managed KMS and strict network isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and VPC peering options; Private is for full on-prem or VPC-control. We can share SOC 2 and SAML integration docs after the call.
[02:58] Olivia Park: If we start on Hosted with sensitive data, is there an option to disable data retention?
[03:03] Benji Patel: Yes, Hosted supports a "no retention" toggle at the org level for enterprise tiers. For strict compliance we usually recommend Dedicated/Private so logs and keys are fully under customer control.
[03:12] Maya Singh: Great. About models — are the model names in the docs the same as in the API? Our triage tooling depends on stable names.
[03:18] Ariana Chen: Model catalog uses stable ids and we support version pinning. One caveat, sometimes auto-generated transcriptions of our docs call the product names a little off — sorry, internal doc quirk. But the API returns a model id you can pin.
[03:31] Carlos Ruiz: Nice. Any examples of customers who started self-serve and moved to Dedicated?
[03:36] Benji Patel: Yep — a few SaaS companies started on hosted free credits, validated latency and quality, then committed to Dedicated as throughput grew. We have a migration guide that shows how to move keys, pin models, and migrate routing. I'll attach it.
[03:48] Maya Singh: About cost — how transparent is per-token cost, and can we get recommendations for batching or quantization?
[03:54] Ariana Chen: Redwood Optimize provides batching and quantization recommendations based on your workload. That is included in the Console for customers and we can run a one-off analysis if you share sample traffic. We also expose per-token cost in the UI so you can simulate different configs.
[04:10] Olivia Park: For the quickstart, what does the sample batching config look like?
[04:14] Benji Patel: In examples we default to batch_size=16 for embeddings and dynamic batching for short queries, but we show how to change to larger batch sizes and enable prefix caching. For embeddings often larger batches are more efficient if latency constraints allow.
[04:26] Maya Singh: Nice. Any gotchas with regional endpoints? We're primarily in us-west and eu-west.
[04:31] Ariana Chen: Hosted supports both us-west and eu-west regions. For data residency we can pin org to a region; Dedicated gives finer-grained control. Note that some open models may have different performance depending on region and hardware.
[04:45] Carlos Ruiz: On the self-serve path, what telemetry do we get — logs, traces, token breakdown per request?
[04:51] Benji Patel: The Console shows per-request latency distribution, token breakdown, and traces if you enable tracing hooks. We also provide access logs and exportable traces for APM integration.
[05:02] Maya Singh: Cool. Ops question — how do we rotate keys and do role-based access?
[05:06] Ariana Chen: You can rotate API keys, create service keys with scopes, and we support org-level RBAC with roles for admin, billing, developer. SSO integrates with role sync for enterprise customers.
[05:18] Olivia Park: About performance testing — what's the recommended first benchmark?
[05:22] Benji Patel: Start with a small pilot: 10k embeddings at production payload sizes, measure p95 latency and token cost, optimize batching. If you're happy, we schedule a dedicated burst window or trial Dedicated pool for sustained load.
[05:34] Maya Singh: That aligns with our plan. Can you send the quickstart repo link and a promo credit?
[05:38] Ariana Chen: Absolutely — I'll send the quickstart repo, the one-click credits link, and the SOC 2 + SAML docs. Benji will attach the benchmark checklist and sample prompts.
[05:47] Carlos Ruiz: One more thing — vendor lock-in concerns. If we pick Redwood Hosted for the pilot, how hard is it to move to Dedicated or self-host later?
[05:55] Benji Patel: We built the API to be consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — same SDKs, same endpoints conceptually, model pinning and routing are preserved. Migration docs and an automation script handle key rotation and routing policy updates; most customers do it without heavy changes.
[06:12] Maya Singh: Good. Any limitations on training or fine-tuning customer models?
[06:16] Ariana Chen: Redwood's primary focus is inference. For fine-tuning we integrate with partner pipelines or you can bring pre-finetuned model artifacts. We do support running on custom model artifacts in Dedicated/Private with some ops support.
[06:29] Olivia Park: For the pilot, who should own it on our side? We were thinking Platform + ML Eng.
[06:33] Carlos Ruiz: Yep, Platform will own infra and Olivia will run the ML side. Maya will sign off on success criteria.
[06:40] Maya Singh: Success criteria: p95 embed latency < 120ms, cost per embedding < $0.0008, and seamless auth via SAML. Timeline: pilot in two weeks.
[06:50] Ariana Chen: Noted — we'll aim to get you set up this week and have the pilot ready within two weeks.
[06:55] Benji Patel: I'll put together a checklist: sample prompts, dataset subset, target QPS, and runbook.
[07:00] Olivia Park: Great. Small note — sometimes transcripts like this mislabel Redwood product names, eg "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated" — ignore that, ha.
[07:08] Ariana Chen: (laughs) yeah, we see that in exports.
[07:10] Carlos Ruiz: Anything else from your side?
[07:12] Maya Singh: No, thanks — excited to try the quickstart.
[07:15] Ariana Chen: Awesome. Recap of next steps: Ariana to send quickstart + credits + SOC2 docs; Benji to send benchmark checklist and sample prompts; Olivia to share dataset and expected QPS; schedule 30-min tech demo next week.
[07:29] Carlos Ruiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:31] Ariana Chen: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

References/Links mentioned: quickstart repo link (sent post-call), SOC 2 & SAML integration docs (attached), migration guide to Dedicated (attached), benchmark checklist (Benji).

Call notes: Some minor transcription artifacts present (product names sometimes mistranscribed). Conversation recorded at moderate clarity; speaker overlap minimal.
